source.title: On Thakur's basis conjecture for multiple zeta values in positive characteristic

summary: Chang, Chen and Mishiba prove Thakur's basis conjecture for multiple zeta values over the function field k = F_q(θ): for every weight w, the values ζ_A(s) with s in Thakur's index set I^T_w — tuples of weight w whose entries are at most q, the last one strictly less — form a k-basis of the space Z_w spanned by the MZVs of weight w. Since |I^T_w| = d'_w this gives Todd's dimension conjecture, the analogue of Zagier's conjecture. The proof switches from the MZVs to the special values Li_s(1) of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, which agree with ζ_A(s) on Thakur's index set by Carlitz's identity. On the generation side the authors introduce a formal weight-graded space H on the set of indices carrying the harmonic and q-shuffle products, with realisation maps to k and k_∞ that turn the stuffle and q-shuffle relations into formal identities, and an explicit rewriting operator U^• which preserves the realisations and, after finitely many iterations, pushes any index into Thakur's set; this reproves Ngo Dac's generating theorem effectively and, as a by-product, identifies all k-linear relations among MZVs of a given weight as generated by [s] − U^ζ(s). On the independence side they run the Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion on the period interpretation of CMPL values, reduce a linear relation to a solution of an explicit system of Frobenius difference equations indexed by initial segments, and compute that the solution space of that system has dimension 1 when (q − 1) divides the weight and 0 otherwise, which forces the relation to be trivial. The atlas plans the objects this is built on — the Carlitz module, its period, Anderson t-modules and effective t-motives, the requested depth-one Carlitz evaluation and Papanikolas's difference-Galois theory, all in the roadmap Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values — but nothing beyond depth one: no multiple zeta values in characteristic p, no Carlitz polylogarithms, no q-shuffle algebra and no ABP criterion. The classical analogues (Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures) are planned at PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.9. This repair makes the analytic and appendix constructions explicit, reuses the existing infinity-completion and restricted-series carriers, and records pending DM.2/DM.6/DM.8 suppliers without turning proof closure into an extraction gate.

items.name: Polynomial and rational-function carriers, infinity valuation and valued completion
items.statement: For a finite field F_q, A=F_q[θ] is Polynomial F_q, k=RatFunc F_q, and A_+ is the subtype of monic polynomials. RatFunc.inftyValuation sends nonzero f/g to exp(deg f−deg g) in ℤᵐ⁰; RatFunc.inftyValued supplies its valued structure and RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty its completed field. The paper’s real normalization |θ|_∞=q and its Laurent-series presentation require the comparison in item 71.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2 (Theorem 1.5 of the published version numbers statements by section)

items.name: The completed algebraic closure C_∞ and the algebraic closure of k in it
items.statement: An algebraic closure k̄_∞ of k_∞ is fixed, |·|_∞ is extended to it, C_∞ is the completion of k̄_∞ for |·|_∞, and k̄ denotes the algebraic closure of k inside C_∞.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2
items.note: Single owner DM.2. Request the actual normed completion of an algebraic closure, its algebraic closedness in characteristic p, embeddings and k̄ inside C_∞. The reviewed audit says not built, and the current DM.0–DM.7 packet covers only DM.0. FA.0 does not construct C_∞; planned means a supplier target, not a supplied implementation.

items.name: Thakur's multiple zeta values
items.statement: For an r-tuple of positive integers s = (s_1, …, s_r), ζ_A(s) := Σ 1/(a_1^{s_1} ⋯ a_r^{s_r}) ∈ k_∞, the sum being over a_1, …, a_r ∈ A_+ with |a_1|_∞ > ⋯ > |a_r|_∞; the series converges because |·|_∞ is non-archimedean, and Thakur proved it is non-vanishing. Its weight is wt(s) = Σ s_i and its depth dep(s) = r. For r = 1 these are the Carlitz zeta values.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2, equation (1.2.1)
items.note: The central object of the paper. DM.6 plans Goss/Taelman L-values and requires the Carlitz module to recover its explicit zeta value, so the depth-one values are in the atlas's direction; the multiple values, their weight/depth grading and Thakur's non-vanishing theorem are not planned. The singleton case agrees with the shared depth-one sum requested at DM.6 in item 52; do not implement a second depth-one zeta function.

items.name: Carlitz module and its exponential and period
items.statement: For A=F_q[θ], the Carlitz module is C:t↦θ+τ. Its exponential is F_q-linear with kernel A·π̃ for a chosen fundamental period π̃; use the compatible normalization in item 53.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2 and Section 2.2
items.note: DM.0 owns the module and DM.2 uniformization. The depth-one sum is separately item 52 and the exact q−1 evaluation is requested in item 64: Taelman’s L(C/A,1) alone is not an evaluation for every positive n.

items.name: The algebra of multiple zeta values and Chang's descent theorem
items.statement: Thakur's q-shuffle relations express a product of two MZVs as an F_p-linear combination of MZVs of the same weight, so the k-vector space Z spanned by all MZVs is an algebra; and by the first author's theorem every k̄-linear relation among MZVs comes from k-linear relations among MZVs of the same weight. Hence determining dim_k Z_w is the central problem.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.2 (after Thakur and Chang)
items.note: The structural facts that make the dimension question well posed; neither the q-shuffle algebra nor the descent from k̄ to k is planned in the atlas.

items.name: Classical multiple zeta values, Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures
items.statement: For w ≥ 2 let 𝔷_w be the Q-vector space spanned by the real MZVs of weight w, and set d_0 = 1, d_1 = 0, d_2 = 1 and d_w = d_{w-2} + d_{w-3}. Zagier's conjecture asserts dim_Q 𝔷_w = d_w (the upper bound is a theorem of Terasoma and Goncharov), and Hoffman's basis conjecture asserts that {ζ(s) : s admissible with all s_i ∈ {2,3}, wt(s) = w} is a basis of 𝔷_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Conjectures 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 (published: Conjectures 1.1 and 1.2)
items.note: PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results', which is where Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures live.

items.name: Todd's dimension conjecture
items.statement: For a positive integer w let Z_w be the k-vector space spanned by the MZVs of weight w, and define d'_w = 2^{w-1} for 1 ≤ w < q, d'_q = 2^{q-1} − 1, and d'_w = Σ_{i=1}^{q} d'_{w-i} for w > q. Then dim_k Z_w = d'_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Conjecture 1.2.2 (published: Conjecture 1.3; after Todd's numerical computations)
items.note: The function-field analogue of Zagier's conjecture; proved in this paper as a consequence of Thakur's basis conjecture.

items.name: Thakur's basis conjecture
items.statement: For a positive integer w let I^T_w be the set of tuples s = (s_1, …, s_r) of positive integers with wt(s) = w, s_i ≤ q for 1 ≤ i ≤ r − 1 and s_r < q. Then B^T_w := {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a basis of the k-vector space Z_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Conjecture 1.2.3 (published: Conjecture 1.4; after Thakur)
items.note: The function-field analogue of Hoffman's basis conjecture, and the main theorem of the paper; |I^T_w| = d'_w, so it implies Todd's conjecture.

items.name: The main theorem
items.statement: For every positive integer w, Thakur's basis conjecture holds; consequently Todd's dimension conjecture holds.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 1.2.4 (published: Theorem 1.5)
items.note: The paper's main result. Its proof has two halves: a generation half, which makes the candidate set span, and a linear-independence half through the ABP criterion.

items.name: Ngo Dac's upper bound
items.statement: For each w ≥ 1 the set B^T_w is a generating set of the k-vector space Z_w, so dim_k Z_w ≤ d'_w. The present paper reproves this in Corollary 3.2.5, in a form that also gives a generating set for the space spanned by the values Li_s(1).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Remark 1.2.5 (published: Remark 1.6; after Ngo Dac)
items.note: The half of the conjecture that was known; the paper's contribution on this side is a concrete and effective algorithm rather than a new bound.

items.name: Descent of the basis to k̄
items.statement: Since k-linear independence of MZVs implies k̄-linear independence, for each positive integer w the set B^T_w is also a basis for the k̄-vector space spanned by the MZVs of weight w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Remark 1.2.6 (published: Remark 1.7)
items.note: Uses the first author's theorem quoted above.

items.name: An upper bound for v-adic multiple zeta values
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of k. For w>0 let Z_{v,w} be the k-vector space spanned by the v-adic MZVs of weight w. Then dim_k Z_{v,w} ≤ d′_w−d′_{w−(q−1)}, with d′_0=1 and d′_n=0 for n<0. The corresponding k̄-span satisfies the bound with dim_{k̄}, not dim_k.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Corollary 1.2.7 (published: Corollary 1.8)
items.note: Corrected coefficient field: E5. The natural k-linear specialization is a surjective graded algebra map onto the k-span. Its kernel contains the ideal generated by ζ_A(q−1). Multiplication by this nonzero element embeds Z_{w−(q−1)} into Z_w; take Z_0=k and negative weight spaces zero. Rank-nullity gives the bound. For the k̄-span, extend a finite k-spanning family; do not regard its dimension over k as finite.

items.name: The parallel work on alternating multiple zeta values
items.statement: Independently and at the same time, Im, Kim, Le, Ngo Dac and Pham proved the corresponding results for alternating MZVs, by studying the k-vector space spanned by the values Li_s(γ_1, …, γ_r) with s ∈ I^T_w and γ_i ∈ F_{q^{q-1}}^×; the primary methods, rooted in Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas, Chang, Todd, Chang–Papanikolas–Yu and Ngo Dac, are the same, with different presentations.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Remark 1.4.1 (published: Remark 1.10)
items.note: Recorded because the two papers together fix the state of the art, and because the atlas will want both in the same roadmap.

items.name: Indices and the graded vector space of indices
items.statement: An index is the empty tuple ∅ or an r-tuple of positive integers, with dep(∅) = wt(∅) = 0, dep(s) = r and wt(s) = Σ s_i; I = ⊔_{r≥0} Z_{≥1}^r is the set of indices, with subsets I_w (weight w), I_{>0}, I^T_w (s_i ≤ q for i < r and s_r < q) and IND_w (q ∤ s_i for all i), and I^T_0 = IND_0 = {∅}. H = ⊕_{w≥0} H_w is the k-vector space with basis I graded by weight, [s] the generator attached to s, and Supp(P) the set of indices with nonzero coefficient in P.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 2.1
items.note: The formal combinatorial framework in which both products and both realisations are defined; nothing analogous is planned in the atlas.

items.name: Thakur's and Ngo Dac's index sets have the same size
items.statement: For each weight w ≥ 0 there is a bijection between IND_w and I^T_w, given by (m_1 q + n_1, …, m_r q + n_r) ↔ (q^{{m_1}}, n_1, …, q^{{m_r}}, n_r) with m_i ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ n_i ≤ q − 1; hence |IND_w| = |I^T_w|.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Proposition 2.1.1 (published: Proposition 2.1)
items.note: The combinatorial identity that lets the linear independence proved for one index set be transported to Thakur's basis.

items.name: Concatenation and the multilinear bracket
items.statement: For indices s_1, …, s_ℓ, (s_1, …, s_ℓ) denotes their concatenation; for a non-empty index s = (s_1, …, s_r) one writes s_+ = (s_1, …, s_{r-1}) and s_- = (s_2, …, s_r). The k-multilinear map [−, …, −] : H^{⊕ℓ} → H is defined on indices by concatenation, so that [s, 0] = 0 while [s, ∅] ≠ 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 2.1.4 and Remark 2.1.5 (published: Definition 2.2 and Remark 2.3)
items.note: The bookkeeping operations on H used in every formula of Sections 2 and 3.

items.name: Carlitz polylogarithms and Carlitz multiple polylogarithms
items.statement: With L_0 = 1 and L_d = (θ − θ^q) ⋯ (θ − θ^{q^d}), the Carlitz logarithm is log_C(z) = Σ_{d≥0} z^{q^d}/L_d, the n-th Carlitz polylogarithm of Anderson–Thakur is Li_n(z) = Σ_{d≥0} z^{q^d}/L_d^n, and for an index s of positive depth the s-th Carlitz multiple polylogarithm (CMPL) is Li_s(z_1, …, z_r) = Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0} z_1^{q^{d_1}} ⋯ z_r^{q^{d_r}} / (L_{d_1}^{s_1} ⋯ L_{d_r}^{s_r}).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 2.2, equation (2.2.1)
items.note: DM.8 plans Carlitz logarithms and their algebraic independence after Papanikolas; the polylogarithms of Anderson–Thakur and their multiple version, introduced by the first author, are the objects this paper actually works with and are not planned.

items.name: Power sums and the three realisation maps
items.statement: For s ≥ 1 and d ≥ 0 put S^{Li}_d(s) := 1/L_d^s and S^ζ_d(s) := Σ_{a ∈ A_{+,d}} 1/a^s, where A_{+,d} is the set of monic polynomials of degree d. For • ∈ {Li, ζ} the k-linear maps 𝔏^•_d, 𝔏^•_{<d} : H → k and 𝔏^• : H → k_∞ are defined by the corresponding sums over d = d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0, over d > d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0 and over d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0, with the conventions on ∅; they satisfy 𝔏^•_d = 𝔏^•_{<d+1} − 𝔏^•_{<d}, 𝔏^• = lim_d 𝔏^•_{<d}, 𝔏^{Li}(s) = Li_s(1) and 𝔏^ζ(s) = ζ_A(s).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 2.2.2 with the identities after it (published: Definition 2.4)
items.note: The formal separation of the two realisations — CMPL values and MZVs — on the same space of indices, which is what lets one algorithm serve both.

items.name: Carlitz's identity and the agreement of the two realisations
items.statement: For 1 ≤ s ≤ q and d ≥ 0 one has 1/L_d^s = Σ_{a ∈ A_{+,d}} 1/a^s (Carlitz); hence for an index s with 1 ≤ s_i ≤ q for all i one has 𝔏^{Li}_d(s) = 𝔏^ζ_d(s), 𝔏^{Li}_{<d}(s) = 𝔏^ζ_{<d}(s) and Li_s(1) = ζ_A(s).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Remark 2.2.12 (published: Remark 2.5)
items.note: The identity that makes Thakur's basis a set of CMPL values, which is what the linear independence argument can handle.

items.name: The harmonic product
items.statement: The harmonic product * = *^{Li} is the k-bilinear map H × H → H with [∅] * P = P * [∅] = P and [s] * [n] = [s_1, s_- * n] + [n_1, s * n_-] + [s_1 + n_1, s_- * n_-]; one sets D^{Li}_{s,n} := 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 2.3
items.note: The stuffle product, which the CMPL realisation preserves.

items.name: Chen's formula and the q-shuffle product
items.statement: H.-J. Chen proved 𝔏^ζ_d(s)𝔏^ζ_d(n) = 𝔏^ζ_d(s+n) + Σ_{j=1}^{s+n-1} Δ^{[j]}_{s,n} 𝔏^ζ_d(s+n−j, j), where Δ^{[j]}_{s,n} = (−1)^{s-1}C(j−1, s−1) + (−1)^{n-1}C(j−1, n−1) if (q−1) | j and 1 ≤ j < s + n, and 0 otherwise. The q-shuffle product *^ζ on H is the k-bilinear map with [∅] *^ζ P = P and [s] *^ζ [n] = [s_1, s_- *^ζ n] + [n_1, s *^ζ n_-] + [s_1 + n_1, s_- *^ζ n_-] + D^ζ_{s,n}, where D^ζ_{s,n} = Σ_{j=1}^{s_1+n_1-1} Δ^{[j]}_{s_1,n_1} [s_1 + n_1 − j, (j) *^ζ (s_- *^ζ n_-)]; both products preserve the weight grading.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 2.3, equations (2.3.2)–(2.3.4) (after H.-J. Chen and Thakur)
items.note: The function-field shuffle: unlike the classical case it is not a shuffle of words, and the correction term D^ζ is what makes the combinatorics of Section 3 delicate.

items.name: Vanishing of the correction term in low weight
items.statement: If s + n ≤ q then Δ^{[j]}_{s,n} = 0 for all j; hence for indices s, n of positive depth with s_1 + n_1 ≤ q one has D^ζ_{s,n} = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Remark 2.3.4 (published: Remark 2.6)
items.note: The reason Thakur's index set, where the entries are ≤ q, is so well behaved.

items.name: The realisations are algebra maps
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Proposition 2.3.5 (published: Proposition 2.7)
items.note: The formal statement that the stuffle relations for CMPLs and the q-shuffle relations for MZVs are realisations of the two products on H.

items.name: The box-plus operator
items.statement: ⊞ : H^{⊕2} → H is the k-linear map with ∅ ⊞ P = P ⊞ ∅ = 0 and s ⊞ n := (s_+, s_r + n_1, n_-) for indices s = (s_+, s_r) and n = (n_1, n_-) of positive depth; in depth one, (s) ⊞ (n) = [s + n], and (n) ⊞ P ≠ [n] + P in general.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 3.1.1 and Remark 3.1.2 (published: Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2)
items.note: The operation that glues the last entry of one index to the first entry of another.

items.name: The Thakur decomposition of an index
items.statement: Every index is written uniquely as s = (s^T, q^{{m}}, s') with s^T ∈ I^T, m ≥ 0 and either s' = ∅ or s'_1 > q; when s' ≠ ∅ one sets s'' := (s'_1 − q, s'_-). For example s = (q−1, q, q, q+1, 1) has s^T = (q−1), m = 2, s' = (q+1, 1) and s'' = (1, 1).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 3.1, equations (3.1.1)–(3.1.2) and Example 3.1.5 (published: Example 3.3)
items.note: The decomposition that measures how far an index is from Thakur's set and drives the induction in Theorem 3.2.4.

items.name: The operators α_q and U^•
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} set α^•_q(P) := [1, (q−1) *^• P], with α^{•,0}_q the identity and α^{•,m}_q its m-th iterate. The k-linear map U^• : H → H is defined on an index s with decomposition (s^T, q^{{m}}, s') by U^•(s) = −[s^T, q^{{m+1}}, s''] + L_1^{m+1}[s^T, α^{•,m+1}_q(s'')] + L_1^{m+1}(s^T ⊞ α^{•,m+1}_q(s'')) − [s^T, q^{{m}}, D^•_{q,s''}] when s' ≠ ∅, and by U^•(s) = L_1^m[s^T, α^{•,m}_q(∅)] + L_1^m(s^T ⊞ α^{•,m}_q(∅)) when s' = ∅. It preserves the weight grading, and U^•(s) = s for s ∈ I^T.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Definition 3.2.2 with Remark 3.2.3 (published: Definition 3.4 and Remark 3.5)
items.note: The explicit rewriting operator; making it explicit, rather than an existence statement, is one of the paper's contributions over earlier work.

items.name: The rewriting algorithm
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and every P ∈ H: (1) 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P); (2) there is an explicit integer e ≥ 0 with Supp((U^•)^e(P)) ⊂ I^T.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 3.2.4 (published: Theorem 3.6)
items.note: The engine of the generation half: iterating U^• rewrites any index into Thakur's set without changing the value. Its proof occupies the appendix.

items.name: Generating sets in both realisations
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and w ≥ 0, let Z^•_w be the k-vector space spanned by the values 𝔏^•(s) for s ∈ I_w. Then {𝔏^•(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a generating set of Z^•_w; in particular Z^{Li}_w = Z^ζ_w = Z_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Corollary 3.2.5 (published: Corollary 3.7)
items.note: Reproves Ngo Dac's generation theorem and, at the same time, identifies the space of MZVs of weight w with the space of CMPL values of weight w.

items.name: The second generating set
items.statement: The k-vector space Z_w is spanned by the values Li_s(1) for s ∈ IND_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 3.2.6 (published: Theorem 3.8)
items.note: The generating set on which the linear independence argument is run, chosen because IND_w is the index set adapted to the Frobenius difference equations.

items.name: Frobenius twisting, the Tate algebra and the ring of entire functions
items.statement: For a new variable t and f = Σ a_i t^i ∈ C_∞((t)) the n-fold Frobenius twist is f^{(n)} := Σ a_i^{q^n} t^i, extended entrywise to matrices; τ^n is an automorphism of C_∞((t)) stabilising C_∞[[t]], the Tate algebra T of power series converging on |t|_∞ ≤ 1, the polynomial rings C_∞[t] and k̄[t] and the fields C_∞(t) and k̄(t), and σ := τ^{-1}. One has T^τ = k̄[t]^τ = F_q[t] = T^σ = k̄[t]^σ and k̄(t)^τ = F_q(t) = k̄(t)^σ. Following ABP, E is the subring of C_∞[[t]] of power series with algebraic coefficients a_i ∈ k̄ such that |a_i|_∞^{1/i} → 0 and [k_∞(a_0, a_1, …) : k_∞] < ∞; such series converge on all of C_∞ and E^τ = F_q[t] = E^σ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 4.1
items.note: DM.8 owns this missing analytic package. Reuse the one-variable restricted carrier at radius 1: over a normed ultrametric ring, IsRestricted 1 f iff ‖coeff n f‖→0, and IsRestricted.subring 1 gives its subring. This supplies neither the normalized C_∞ field nor the Gauss norm, completeness, coefficient twists and their fixed rings, convergence/evaluation or the ABP finite-coefficient-field entire condition. Those remain explicit requests. Read PowerSeries/Restricted.lean at the pin; multivariable restricted series are also available, but do not duplicate the univariate carrier.

items.name: The Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion
items.statement: Let Φ ∈ Mat_ℓ(k̄[t]) be such that det Φ vanishes, if at all, only at t = θ, and let ψ ∈ Mat_{ℓ×1}(E) satisfy ψ^{(-1)} = Φψ. If ρ ∈ Mat_{1×ℓ}(k̄) satisfies ρψ(θ) = 0, then there is 𝒫 ∈ Mat_{1×ℓ}(k̄[t]) with 𝒫ψ = 0 and 𝒫(θ) = ρ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 4.1.1 (published: Theorem 4.1; [ABP04, Theorem 3.1.1])
items.note: DM.8 owns this criterion. The partial DM.8 packet records ABP proof reading as a gap. The accepted source route is now present on issues #1008 and #1009 (checked 2026-09-30); supplying a source is not completion of the theorem. Part II consumes the explicit requested statement and may proceed without awaiting proof closure of every supplier.

items.name: Initial segments, the coefficient ring R and the Frobenius system (E_M)
items.statement: For an index s = (s_1, …, s_r), 𝔦(s) := {∅, (s_1), (s_1, s_2), …, s} and 𝔦(M) := ∪_{s ∈ M} 𝔦(s); R := {f/g : f ∈ k̄[t], g ∈ F_q[t] \ {0}} ⊂ k̄(t). For w ≥ 0 and ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w the system (E_M) of Frobenius equations is ε_s^{(1)} = ε_s (t − θ)^{w − wt(s)} + Σ_{s' > 0, (s, s') ∈ 𝔦(M)} ε_{(s,s')} (t − θ)^{w − wt(s)} for s ∈ 𝔦(M), with (ε_s) ∈ R^{𝔦(M)}. For w = 0 it reduces to ε_∅^{(1)} = ε_∅.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 4.2, equation (E_M), with Remark 4.2.1 (published: Remark 4.2)
items.note: The system is the case Q_i = 1 of Chang–Papanikolas–Yu's equations, written with subscripts indexed by initial segments following Ngo Dac.

items.name: Solutions of a twisted linear equation are polynomial
items.statement: Let F = Σ_{i=0}^n f_i t^i and G lie in A[t] with n = deg_t F ≥ 1 and f_n ∈ F_q^×. If ε ∈ R satisfies ε^{(1)} = εF + G, then ε ∈ F_q(t)[θ].
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma 4.2.2 (published: Lemma 4.3)
items.note: The rationality step: it removes denominators and puts the solutions in a polynomial ring in θ over F_q(t).

items.name: Degree bound for the solutions
items.statement: Let w ≥ 0 and ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w. If (ε_s)_{s ∈ 𝔦(M)} ∈ R^{𝔦(M)} satisfies (E_M), then ε_s ∈ F_q(t)[θ] and deg_θ ε_s ≤ (w − wt(s))/(q − 1) for each s ∈ 𝔦(M).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma 4.2.3 (published: Lemma 4.4)
items.note: The degree bound that makes the solution space finite dimensional and is the source of the divisibility condition by q − 1.

items.name: The index set IND°_w and the system (E_w)
items.statement: IND°_w := {∅} for w = 0 and, for w > 0, the set of (s_1, …, s_r) ∈ IND_w with s_2, …, s_r divisible by q − 1; (E_w) is the system (E_M) for M = IND°_w, and X_w denotes its set of R-valued solutions, an F_q(t)-vector subspace of R^{𝔦(IND°_w)} since f^{(1)} = f for f ∈ F_q(t).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 4.3, equation (4.3.1), Definition 4.3.3 and Remark 4.3.4 (published: Definition 4.6 and Remark 4.7)
items.note: The description of IND°_w comes from the simultaneously Eulerian phenomenon of Chang–Papanikolas–Yu, first observed by Lara Rodríguez and Thakur.

items.name: Worked examples of the Frobenius system
items.statement: For w = 0 the system (E_w) is the single equation ε_∅^{(1)} = ε_∅; for w = q, IND°_q = {(1, q−1)} and 𝔦(IND°_q) = {∅, (1), (1, q−1)} give three equations; for w = 2q − 2 with q ≥ 3, IND°_{2q-2} = {(q−1, q−1), (2q−2)} gives four equations, written out explicitly in the paper.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Example 4.3.2 (published: Example 4.5)
items.note: The acceptance examples for any implementation of the system.

items.name: The dimension of the solution space
items.statement: For every w ≥ 0, dim_{F_q(t)} X_w = 1 if (q − 1) | w and 0 otherwise. When w = ℓ(q − 1) one may choose a generator (η_{ℓ;s}) with η_{ℓ;∅} = Σ_{i=0}^{ℓ} b_{ℓi}(t − θ)^i, where b_{ℓi} ∈ T F_p[T]_{(T)} for 0 ≤ i < ℓ and b_{ℓℓ} = 1, with T := t − t^q and F_p[T]_{(T)} the localisation of F_p[T] at (T).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 4.3.5 (published: Theorem 4.8)
items.note: The key computation of Section 4 and the reason the answer depends only on the congruence of w modulo q − 1.

items.name: Eulerian values
items.statement: A value is Eulerian when it is a k-multiple of a power of the Carlitz period π̃; concretely, Li_P(1) = Σ_s a_s Li_s(1) is Eulerian of weight w when it lies in k · π̃^w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma 5.1.1 (published: Lemma 5.1), second hypothesis
items.note: The Carlitz period π̃ and its transcendence belong to DM.2 and DM.8; the notion of an Eulerian multiple zeta value, and the simultaneously Eulerian phenomenon that shapes IND°_w, are specific to this circle of ideas.

items.name: The key lemma
items.statement: Let w ≥ 0, ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w and P = Σ a_s[s] ∈ H with coefficients in k such that Supp(P) ⊂ M, Li_P(1) is Eulerian, and the values Li_s(1) for s ∈ 𝔦(M) ∩ I_ℓ are k-linearly independent for each 0 ≤ ℓ < w. Then: (1) for each s ∈ 𝔦(M), either Σ_{s' ∈ I_{w-wt(s)}} a_{(s,s')}Li_{s'}(1) = 0 or (q − 1) | (w − wt(s)); in particular, if the relevant values are linearly independent then Supp(P) ⊂ {(s_1, …, s_r) ∈ I_w : (q − 1) | s_2, …, s_r}; and (2) the system (E_M) has a solution (ε_s) ∈ F_q(t)[θ]^{𝔦(M)} with ε_s = a_s|_{θ = t} for each s ∈ M.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma 5.1.1 (published: Lemma 5.1)
items.note: The proof constructs the analytic prefix matrices in §5, applies ABP, eliminates the defect by specialization and lower-weight CMPL descent, then uses fixed-field uniqueness and CPY denominator descent. It handles arbitrary nonempty M⊂I_w; IND°_w is a later specialization.

items.name: Linear independence of the CMPL values
items.statement: For each w ≥ 0 the values Li_s(1) with s ∈ IND_w form a basis of Z_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 5.2.1 (published: Theorem 5.2)
items.note: Induct on w. For w=0 use Z_0=k and Li_empty(1)=1. For w>0, the key lemma maps relations into X_w. When q−1 divides w, item 65 supplies a nonzero representative of π̃^w; dim X_w=1 then forces every zero-valued relation to vanish. The published proof explicitly states π̃^w∈Z_w, where the preprint uses the same input implicitly.

items.name: Proof of the main theorem
items.statement: Since |I^T_w| = |IND_w| (Proposition 2.1.1) and B^T_w generates Z_w (Corollary 3.2.5), while {Li_s(1) : s ∈ IND_w} is a basis of Z_w (Theorem 5.2.1), the set B^T_w is a k-basis of Z_w; hence dim_k Z_w = |I^T_w| = d'_w, which is Todd's conjecture.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 5.3 (proof of Theorem 1.2.4)
items.note: The assembly of the two halves.

items.name: All linear relations among multiple zeta values
items.statement: Let w be a positive integer. All k-linear relations among the MZVs of weight w are generated by the relations [s] − U^ζ(s) for s ∈ I_w \ I^T_w: writing 𝔏^ζ_w : H_w ↠ Z_w for the realisation and R_w := Span_k{[s] − U^ζ(s) : s ∈ I_w \ I^T_w}, one has Ker 𝔏^ζ_w = R_w, and Ker 𝔏^ζ = ⊕_{w ∈ N} R_w. Published Remark 5.4 additionally says that, after scalar extension to k̄, these same relations generate all k̄-linear relations among MZVs; the all-weight assertion uses Chang’s grading and descent theorem.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem 5.4.2 (published: Theorem 5.3); published Remark 5.4, p. 26 (added after v2)
items.note: The effective description of the ideal of relations; it is the mechanism the authors advertise as going beyond earlier work, and it answers a shuffle-version of Todd's Conjecture 5.1.

items.name: Depth bounds for the products
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and indices s, n, every u ∈ Supp(s *^• n) satisfies max{dep(s), dep(n)} ≤ dep(u) ≤ dep(s) + dep(n).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Proposition A.1.1 (published: Proposition A.1)
items.note: The first of the combinatorial estimates that make the rewriting algorithm terminate.

items.name: Depth bounds for the correction terms and for α_q
items.statement: For non-empty indices s, n every u ∈ Supp(D^ζ_{s,n}) satisfies max{dep(s), dep(n)} ≤ dep(u) ≤ dep(s) + dep(n); and for m ≥ 0 every u ∈ Supp(α^{•,m}_q(s)) satisfies dep(u) ≥ 1 + m if s = ∅ and m ≥ 1, dep(u) ≥ dep(s) + m otherwise, and dep(u) ≤ dep(s) + 2m.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Corollary A.1.2 (published: Corollary A.2)
items.note: The bounds used to control the iterates of U^•.

items.name: Binary relations and the spaces P^•_w
items.statement: For •∈{Li,ζ}, P^•={(P,Q)∈H⊕H : 𝔏^•_d(P)+𝔏^•_{d+1}(Q)=0 for every integer d}. For w≥0 define P^•_w=P^•∩(H_w⊕H_w); membership requires both entries homogeneous of weight w. A binary relation implies 𝔏^•(P)+𝔏^•(Q)=0. The basic relation R_1=([q],−L_1[1,q−1]) lies in P^•_q by Thakur 2009 Theorem 5 and Carlitz’s identity, for both realizations.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section A.2 with Example A.2.3 (published: Example A.3)
items.note: The formal calculus of relations between truncated sums at consecutive degrees, from which the identity 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P) is assembled.

api.statement: Membership means vanishing at every integer degree, with the second term at d+1.

items.name: Operations on binary relations
items.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ}, every index s of positive depth and integers m ≥ 0, w > 0, the maps B^•_s, C^•_s and BC^{•,m}_q satisfy B^•_s(P^•_w) ⊂ P^•_{w+wt(s)}, C^•_s(P^•_w) ⊂ P^•_{w+wt(s)} and BC^{•,m}_q(P^•_w) ⊂ P^•_{w+mq}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Proposition A.3.1 (published: Proposition A.4)
items.note: The maps that propagate a binary relation to higher weight, used to prove the first half of Theorem 3.2.4.

items.name: U^• preserves the realisations
items.statement: For each P ∈ H one has 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem A.3.2 (published: Theorem A.5; this is Theorem 3.2.4(1))
items.note: Proved by exhibiting the defining formula of U^• as a combination of binary relations.

items.name: Strict progress of the rewriting
items.statement: Let s ∈ I \ I^T. Then: (1) if n ∈ Supp(U^•_1(s)) then dep(n) > dep(s); (2) if n ∈ Supp(U^•_2(s)) then dep(n) ≥ dep(s) and Init(n) > Init(s) lexicographically; (3) if n ∈ Supp(U^•_3(s)) then dep(n) ≥ dep(s) > ℓ_1 := dep(Init(s)), Init(n) ≥ Init(s) and 1 ≤ n_{ℓ_1+1} < s_{ℓ_1+1}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Lemma A.3.7 (published: Lemma A.6)
items.note: The termination argument: each of the three parts of U^• strictly increases a combinatorial measure.

items.name: Termination of the rewriting algorithm
items.statement: For each P ∈ H there exists e ≥ 0 with Supp((U^•)^e(P)) ⊂ I^T.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Theorem A.3.8 (published: Theorem A.7; this is Theorem 3.2.4(2))
items.note: The second half of Theorem 3.2.4, and with it the effective algorithm expressing any MZV in Thakur's basis.

items.name: Switching from multiple zeta values to CMPL values
items.statement: The proof replaces the study of the MZVs by that of the special values Li_s(1) of Carlitz multiple polylogarithms: by the Anderson–Thakur interpolation formula and the first author's work every ζ_A(s) is a k-linear combination of CMPL values at integral points, and for s ∈ I^T_w one has the identity ζ_A(s) = Li_s(1). The argument then splits into a generation half (Corollary 3.2.5 and Theorem 3.2.6) and a linear-independence half (Theorem 5.2.1) run through the ABP criterion.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.09929v2 (11 July 2022), Section 1.3
items.note: The organising idea of the paper; the Anderson–Thakur interpolation and the polynomials it rests on are inputs from the literature that the atlas does not cover.

items.name: Analytic realization and ABP lifting for arbitrary prefix sets
items.statement: For w>0, nonempty M⊂I_w and a finitely supported family a_s∈k supported on M, clear denominators so α_s(t)=a_s|_{θ=t} lies in F_q[t]. Items 62–63 construct Φ′, Ψ′, Φ, Ψ, Φ̃ and ψ̃ on J=I(M)\M, satisfying Ψ^{(−1)}=ΦΨ and ψ̃^{(−1)}=Φ̃ψ̃, with ψ̃∈E^{|J|+2} and det Φ̃ a power of t−θ. If Σ a_s Li_s(1)=cπ̃^w with c∈k, then (−c,0,…,0,1)ψ̃(θ)=0 and ABP yields a polynomial lift; dividing by its last coefficient produces a rational row (g,g_s,1), regular at θ, with that specialization and (g,g_s,1)ψ̃=0.
items.locator: Published §5.1, proof of Lemma 5.1, pp.22–24; preprint proof of Lemma 5.1.1; §1.3(II-1)
items.note: The matrices are actually constructed in the paper. Remark 1.9 (v2 Remark 1.3.2) omits the dual t-motive interpretation, not this analytic construction. Use DM.4 for any motive packaging and DM.8 for the shared analytic criteria; Part II owns the indexed CMPL construction.

items.name: Depth-one Carlitz zeta sum
items.statement: For n>0, ζ_A(n)=Σ_{a∈A_+}a^(−n)=Σ_{d≥0}S^ζ_d(n)∈k_∞, the depth-one specialization of the convergent Thakur MZV. Z_0=k is the separate empty-index convention.
items.note: DM.6 owns the depth-one sum and its convergence; item 3 agrees with it at singleton indices. Do not make the supplier definition depend on Part II.

items.name: Ω and the compatible Carlitz period
items.statement: Choose λ∈k̄ with λ^(q−1)=−θ. Put Ω(t)=λ^(−q)∏_{i≥1}(1−t/θ^(q^i)). Then Ω is an entire series with algebraic coefficients in a finite extension of k_∞, is a unit on the closed unit disc, satisfies Ω^{(−1)}=(t−θ)Ω, Ω has simple zeros exactly at θ^(q^j), j≥1, and π̃=1/Ω(θ).
items.locator: §5 opening, pp.21–22; ABP §3.1.2; Papanikolas §3.3.4
items.note: Import the accepted PAPER-NGODAC-21/omega and align PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/omega-and-carlitz-period. DM.8 currently requests π_P=−1/Ω(θ), matching Papanikolas. For the same Ω, π_P=−π̃ (c=−1∈F_q^×); Eulerian lines agree, while normalized weight-w values differ by c^(−w). A different root gives a general F_q^× scalar, which must also be recorded. DM.2 exports these series/analytic properties; DM.8 identifies them with its T and E predicates. The Ω construction does not acquire a reverse dependency on the DM.8 difference-Galois layer.

items.name: Entire convergence of the CMPL deformation
items.statement: For every positive index s, the series 𝓛(s) of item 55 converges in T and lies in E, including the finite extension condition on its algebraic coefficients. The empty index has the same membership.
items.locator: §5 p.22, citing Chang 2014 Lemma 5.3.1
items.note: One cited analytic result under §16. General analytic proof infrastructure stays with DM.8; specialize the generic CMPL result to Q_i=1.

items.name: Specialization along the Frobenius orbit
items.statement: For every index s and every j≥0, 𝓛(s)(θ^(q^j))=(Li_s(1)/π̃^wt(s))^(q^j). Evaluation uses the entire representative, even when θ^(q^j) is outside the unit disc.
items.locator: §5 p.22; CPY Proposition 2.3.3 and Chang Lemma 5.3.5

items.name: Carlitz period power criterion
items.statement: For n>0, π̃^n∈k_∞ iff q−1 divides n. Indeed π̃∈λ·k_∞^× with λ^(q−1)=−θ. Thus if a nonzero Z∈k_∞ satisfies Z/π̃^n∈k, then q−1 divides n. The n=0 case is 1∈k.
items.locator: Lemma 5.1 proof, p.24
items.note: Import PAPER-NGODAC-21/period-power; compare the stronger constant-field Laurent-series obstruction in PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/pi-power-outside-Fqbar-laurent. No duplicate proof owner.

items.name: Fixed field of the Tate fraction field
items.statement: For L=Frac(T) with coefficient inverse-q-Frobenius σ, L^σ=F_q(t).
items.locator: Papanikolas Lemma 3.3.2, p.12; used by CCM §5.1 p.24
items.note: DM.8 request; the current packet explicitly lists this as an analytic gap. Fixed elements of k̄(t) alone do not establish this larger fixed field.

items.name: Fundamental matrices differ by a constant matrix
items.statement: Let Φ∈GL_r(k̄(t)) and Ψ,X∈GL_r(Frac(T)) satisfy Ψ^{(−1)}=ΦΨ and X^{(−1)}=ΦX. Then X=Ψν for a unique ν∈GL_r(F_q(t)). More generally a rectangular solution X has ν=Ψ^(−1)X with entries in F_q(t).
items.locator: Papanikolas §4.1.6, p.22; CCM Lemma 5.1 proof p.24
items.note: Reuse PAPER-NGODAC-21/trivialization-uniqueness, now explicitly depending on the Frac(T) fixed field. Compute σ(Ψ^(−1)X)=Ψ^(−1)X.

items.name: Frobenius-invariant common denominator
items.statement: For i=1,2, let Φ_i∈Mat_(r_i)(k̄[t]) with det Φ_i=c_i(t−θ)^(m_i), c_i∈k̄^× and m_i≥0. If F∈Mat_(r_1×r_2)(k̄(t)) satisfies F^{(−1)}Φ_2=Φ_1F, its monic least common denominator belongs to F_q[t]. In particular a nonzero b∈F_q[t] clears all its denominators.
items.locator: CPY Proposition 2.2.1, preprint p.6; CCM equation (5.2) and Lemma 5.1(2), p.24
items.note: Import PAPER-NGODAC-21/constant-denominator and its existing E10 correction: F is rational, as the module-map domain and proof require, although CPY prints polynomial entries. Retain both determinant hypotheses. This fix does not create a second CPY erratum.

items.name: Prefix matrices for an arbitrary set of weight-w indices
items.statement: Let w>0, ∅≠M⊂I_w, J=I(M)\M, and α_s∈F_q[t] finitely supported on M. For n,s∈J set Φ′_(n,s)=(t−θ)^(w−wt(s)) if s=n or s=n_+, and 0 otherwise. Set Ψ′_(n,s)=𝓛(u)Ω^(w−wt(n)) if n=(s,u), and 0 otherwise. Define v_s=α_(s,w−wt(s))(t−θ)^(w−wt(s)) when (s,w−wt(s))∈M, and 0 otherwise; f_s=Σ_{u∈I_(w−wt(s))}α_(s,u)𝓛(u). Put Φ=((Φ′,0),(v,1)), Ψ=((Ψ′,0),(f,1)). Then Ψ∈GL_(|J|+1)(T), Ψ^{(−1)}=ΦΨ, and det Φ=(t−θ)^Σ_{s∈J}(w−wt(s)).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.1, pp.22–23; v2 Lemma 5.1.1

items.name: Descent of independence for CMPL values
items.statement: Let w_1,…,w_ℓ be distinct positive integers and let V_i be a finite set of weight-w_i monomials in nonzero CMPL values at algebraic points in their convergence domains. routes.title: Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values, Part II: multiple zeta values and Thakur's basis
routes.brief: Plan multiple zeta values in positive characteristic and the proof of Thakur's basis conjecture by Chang, Chen and Mishiba. The final theorems are: (1) their Theorem 1.2.4 (Theorem 1.5 of the published version): for every positive integer w, Thakur's basis conjecture holds — with A = F_q[θ], k = F_q(θ), k_∞ = F_q((1/θ)) and ζ_A(s) = Σ_{|a_1|>⋯>|a_r|, a_i monic} a_1^{-s_1} ⋯ a_r^{-s_r}, the set {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a k-basis of the space Z_w spanned by the MZVs of weight w, where I^T_w consists of the tuples of weight w with s_i ≤ q for i < r and s_r < q; and consequently Todd's dimension conjecture holds, dim_k Z_w = d'_w with d'_w = 2^{w-1} for w < q, d'_q = 2^{q-1} − 1 and d'_w = Σ_{i=1}^q d'_{w-i} for w > q; (2) their Theorem 5.4.2 (published Theorem 5.3): all k-linear relations among the MZVs of weight w are generated by [s] − U^ζ(s) for s ∈ I_w \ I^T_w, so that the kernel of the realisation map is ⊕_w R_w. The roadmap must cover: Thakur's multiple zeta values with their weight and depth, their non-vanishing, the q-shuffle relations and the resulting algebra structure, and the descent of k̄-linear relations to k-linear relations of fixed weight; Carlitz polylogarithms and Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, the power sums S^{Li}_d and S^ζ_d, and Carlitz's identity 1/L_d^s = Σ_{a ∈ A_{+,d}} a^{-s} which makes ζ_A(s) = Li_s(1) on Thakur's index set; the formal framework — the weight-graded space H on the set of indices, the harmonic and q-shuffle products with H.-J. Chen's formula for the correction terms, and the three realisation maps 𝔏^•_d, 𝔏^•_{<d}, 𝔏^• with the theorem that they are algebra maps; the rewriting calculus — the box-plus operator, the decomposition s = (s^T, q^{{m}}, s'), the operators α_q and U^•, the theorem that U^• preserves the realisations and terminates in Thakur's index set, and the generating sets that follow; the Frobenius-difference machinery — the system (E_M), the rationality and degree bounds for its solutions, the index set IND°_w coming from the simultaneously Eulerian phenomenon, and the computation that the solution space X_w has dimension 1 when (q − 1) | w and 0 otherwise; the key lemma turning a linear relation among CMPL values into a solution of that system; and the assembly of the two halves into the basis theorem and the description of all linear relations. The appendix material — depth bounds, binary relations and the operators on them — is part of the rewriting calculus and must be planned with it. Import, and do not re-plan: the Carlitz module, additive polynomials and the Ore ring from Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values (DrinfeldModulesAndTModules), stage DM.0; analytic uniformisation, the Carlitz exponential and the period π̃ from DM.2; Anderson t-modules and effective t-motives with their τ-action and rigid analytic triviality from DM.4; the requested q−1 Carlitz evaluation (item 64) from DM.6; and the Frobenius-difference setting — twisting, the Tate algebra, the ABP ring E, the ABP criterion and Papanikolas's Tannakian difference-Galois theory — from DM.8, to which this paper is also routed as a source for the criterion itself. Import global function fields and their constants from Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic), stage FA.0. The classical analogues — real multiple zeta values, Zagier's dimension conjecture and Hoffman's basis conjecture, with shuffle, stuffle and regularisation — are planned in Periods, motivic L-values and special-value conjectures (PeriodsAndSpecialValues), stage PS.9, and should be cited for orientation but not re-planned. Keep the Anderson–Thakur interpolation and polynomial inputs shared with the joined Ngo Dac extraction. Section 5 itself constructs the CMPL deformation and prefix matrices: plan items 54–57 and 62–63, then item 51’s ABP lift for arbitrary M. Use the Q_i=1 specialization, not an identification with Ngo Dac’s Ω–H series. Import Ω and its positive reciprocal period, the period-power criterion and C_∞ from DM.2; compare the DM.8 Papanikolas convention by its F_q^× scalar. Request the Frac(T) fixed field, matrix uniqueness and rational common denominator from DM.8, retaining both determinant hypotheses. Plan item 65 to deduce π̃^w∈Z_w using only the q−1 evaluation and graded multiplication, with Z_0=k handled separately. Include the explicit B, C, BC, Init and U_1,U_2,U_3 definitions (items 66–70) and the all-weight/homogeneous binary-relation distinction. Corollary 1.8 concerns the k-span with dim_k; published Remark 5.4 is the k̄-linear consequence of the existing descent theorem. Shared supplier requests record pending mathematical work, not completed imports. The design can proceed with these explicit requests; completion of every parent blueprint is not an extraction or design-start gate.
routes.reason: The atlas plans the objects this paper is built on — the Carlitz module (DM.0), its analytic uniformisation and period (DM.2), Anderson t-modules and effective t-motives (DM.4), the requested Carlitz evaluation (DM.6) and Papanikolas's Frobenius-difference Galois theory with Carlitz logarithms (DM.8) — but stops at depth one and at logarithms. Thakur's multiple zeta values, Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, the q-shuffle algebra, the rewriting calculus that produces Thakur's basis and the Frobenius systems that prove its linear independence are new layers in exactly that roadmap's direction, so this is a Part II of it rather than a new roadmap: it imports DM.0–DM.8 and adds the higher-depth theory. The classical counterpart is planned separately at PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.9 and is not re-planned here.

DM.8 plans the Frobenius-difference machinery of characteristic-p transcendence: the Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial t-motives, the analytic trivialisation matrix and the specialisation/lifting criterion identifying the period transcendence degree with the dimension of the difference-Galois group, after Papanikolas. That theory is built on the Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas linear independence criterion and on the standard twisting setting — the n-fold Frobenius twist on C_∞((t)), the Tate algebra, the ABP ring E of entire functions with algebraic coefficients and the fixed rings F_q[t] and F_q(t) — neither of which the layer states. Both belong inside DM.8, and this paper is a source for them; the Part II then imports them rather than restating them. Also request Frac(T)^σ=F_q(t), fundamental-matrix comparison and CPY’s common-denominator theorem. Reuse the accepted Ngo Dac source items; the current packet remains partial.

C_∞, the normalized infinity completion and Laurent comparison, Ω/period compatibility and the period-power criterion share the analytic-uniformization owner. Reuse Ngo Dac’s accepted DM.2 items and reconcile the sign with the DM.8 request.
Request precisely ζ_A(q−1)=−(θ^q−θ)^(−1)π̃^(q−1), sharing PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/carlitz-zeta-q-minus-1. Taelman’s class-number target alone did not explicitly supply it.
